segments.title: Chương 54: 0054 [Mỗi người một chú mèo nhỏ]
segments.content:
This year, the Gregorian and Lunar calendars were close together. January 21st was New Year's Eve.

Once New Year's Day passed, the end of the semester arrived in the blink of an eye.

The night before the exams, it suddenly started to sleet.

If you held out your hand to catch it, you could vaguely see snowflakes, which would melt into water within a second or two.

But it got the students incredibly excited. From the male and female dorms and apartments, countless students shouted, "It's snowing!" People cheered and ran outside, jumping around in the light rain. The scene would have made anyone from the north laugh themselves silly.

Even until the exams the next day, everyone was still talking about last night's snow.

After four exams, Chen Guiliang felt he had made noticeable progress.

Especially in math. Even though the questions were harder than the monthly test, he was confident he could score over 80.

After the last exam, Liberal Arts Comprehensive, everyone hurried to catch their buses home, not even bothering with a farewell meal.

The first semester of senior year ended just like that, without a sound.

Chen Guiliang stayed one more night in the dorm. He still had to go buy a cat with Bian Guanyue tomorrow.

What would be the county's flower and bird market ten years from now was currently a street full of KTVs.

Commonly known as "Struggle Street."

The "struggle" in its name meant a final, agonizing struggle before death.

In the Fushi County of 2004, there didn't seem to be any specialty shops for flowers, birds, or pets.

Chen Guiliang packed his luggage and took a bus to West Lake.

The so-called West Lake was actually just a stinky pond. In the summer, when the lotuses were in full bloom, it was exceptionally beautiful. In the winter, it was all mud, sewage, withered branches, dead leaves, and household trash.

It wasn't particularly dirty this year because it had been cleaned up once last year during a dry spell, and they had even mobilized students from No. 2 Middle School as volunteers.

Next to West Lake was a mountain, upon which lay the tomb of Liu Guangdi, one of the Six Gentlemen of the Wuxu Reform.

At the foot of the mountain, circling the lake, were all sorts of shops and stalls.

Bian Guanyue's maternal grandparents lived less than a kilometer from West Lake, so she had strolled over.

The two had arranged to meet in front of a music store.

When Chen Guiliang arrived, Bian Guanyue was idly browsing through cassette tapes.

"Whose songs did you buy?" Chen Guiliang asked as he walked into the store.

Bian Guanyue said, "Xiao Xiao and Chen Lin's."

Chen Guiliang wasn't familiar with either of them. "I know Chen Lin, 'Happy Old Home,' right? Who's Xiao Xiao?"

Bian Guanyue corrected him, "'Happy Old Home' is by Chen Ming..."

"Haha, they're both named Chen, same as my family name." Chen Guiliang laughed heartily, not the least bit embarrassed.

He picked up the cassette to look at the song titles and realized he had actually heard two of them.

One was Chen Lin's "Don't Want to Lie to Myself," and the other was Xiao Xiao's "Love Must Be Forthright."

Bian Guanyue paid for the tapes.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Don't you listen to music on an MP3 player?"

Bian Guanyue said, "I also have a language repeater. I usually use it to listen to English, but occasionally for music too. The sound quality of an MP3 player is actually not as good as a cassette tape in a repeater."

"I'm not that particular. It all sounds the same to me," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue went along with him, "The difference isn't that big."

"Then let me borrow your MP3 player. I can listen to music on the train to pass the time." Chen Guiliang didn't treat himself as an outsider.

Bian Guanyue immediately took out her MP3 player and handed it to him. "It uses a triple-A battery. You'd better buy a spare before you get on the train."

How primitive, it wasn't even rechargeable.

Chen Guiliang stuffed the MP3 player into his pants pocket. "West Lake is close to your home, you must come here often, right?"

Bian Guanyue recalled her childhood memories, "When I was little, I'd come back to Fushi County every summer vacation, and my grandparents would bring me here to play. I remember there was an amusement park on the mountain."

"The amusement park went out of business," Chen Guiliang said, bursting her bubble. "Only the Martyrs' Cemetery and Liu Guangdi's Tomb still have people visiting to pay respects."

Bian Guanyue fell silent for a moment. Another piece of her childhood had been chipped away.

Passing by a ring toss stall, Bian Guanyue remembered how her grandparents used to bring her here to play when she was little.

Seeing her slow down, Chen Guiliang immediately took out some money and said, "Boss, give me twenty rings!"

The stall owner was squatting on a folding stool, flipping through a low-quality pirated magazine. Hearing this, he stood up gleefully to take the money.

Bian Guanyue was a little hesitant.

She felt that ring toss was too childish, something only little girls would like.

Chen Guiliang pushed the rings into her hands. "Ten each. Let's see who can get more."

"Okay," Bian Guanyue accepted the rings.

A few minutes later, someone became rather childish...

"Ah, so close!"

"Are you any good at this? You've already thrown all my rings."

"I am, I am, just don't distract me."

"Not enough rings."

"Buy twenty more."

"..."

The stall owner beamed, watching the two suckers with a gratified look.

"I got it, I got one! Haha."

Bian Guanyue hooked a keychain and celebrated with a punch in the air.

Where was even a hint of her usual composure?

The stall owner said, "The ones on the ground are just samples, you can pick a new one."

Bian Guanyue went over and spent a good while choosing, finally picking a keychain with a little plastic pig on it.

This was her prize.

Then, she pretended nothing had happened, reverting to her mature high school student persona, waiting for Chen Guiliang to finish throwing the remaining rings.

As they walked along the lake, they passed several stalls selling cats and dogs.

Chen Guiliang mainly looked at their fur and condition, stopping at one stall. "How old is this litter of kittens?"

The stall owner said, "Almost three months. Born from my own cat, not those 'weekend cats.' 3 yuan for one, 5 for two, or you can take all five for 10 yuan."

"You pick first," Chen Guiliang said to Bian Guanyue.

Bian Guanyue squatted down to look closely and quickly took a liking to a calico.

Chen Guiliang took out five yuan and said, "The black and white one and the calico."

The stall owner put the two kittens into a used shopping bag. He didn't sell cat carriers or cat food.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Where's a pet clinic?"

The stall owner said, "Never heard of it. What's a pet clinic? If you walk all the way down this road, there's a pet shop at the far end of West Lake."

Bian Guanyue volunteered to carry the bag, stroking the kittens' ears from time to time.

At the pet shop, when the owner heard they were newly bought kittens, he advised them to wait a few days before bathing and deworming them.

He was afraid the kittens would get stressed.

He did, however, sell them a carrier, a litter box, and cat food.

As they passed a noodle shop, Chen Guiliang asked, "Did you have breakfast?"

"No." Bian Guanyue had actually already eaten.

The two went inside with the kittens. Chen Guiliang said, "I'll have a bowl of beef noodles. What are you having?"

Bian Guanyue scanned the menu on the wall, "A bowl of Jipotou."

Before the noodles even arrived, Bian Guanyue squatted down to tease the kittens.

Chen Guiliang reminded her, "Don't scare them. Wait a few days after you get them home to play with them."

"Oh."

Bian Guanyue sat back down on the stool, her eyes constantly darting toward the cat carrier.

"Jipotou is here!"

Bian Guanyue picked up her chopsticks and asked Chen Guiliang, "Why is it called Jipotou? In Rongcheng they call it Pugai Mian."

Chen Guiliang ladled half a bowl of free soup and, dipping his finger in it, wrote some obscure characters on the table: 齑馎饦.

"These three characters are pronounced 'jī bó tuō.' Doesn't it sound a lot like 'jī pó tóu'?" Chen Guiliang smiled.

It dawned on Bian Guanyue. "I always thought it was strange when I was little, but no one could explain it clearly. Now I finally understand."

"This type of noodle is very ancient," Chen Guiliang explained eloquently. "Lu You wrote a poem, and two lines from it are: 'A bowl of Jibotuo, and my old belly swells.' Lu You was saying that after eating a bowl of Jipotou, his old stomach was all bloated."

"You're tricking me again," Bian Guanyue didn't believe him.

Chen Guiliang said, "It's true. Lu You was demoted and served as an official in Rongzhou."

Seeing how serious he was, Bian Guanyue couldn't quite tell if he was telling the truth.

Chen Guiliang also often lamented that while Longdu was always trying to build itself up as a tourist city with food being a major highlight,

their cultural and creative efforts were terrible. They'd even claim the origin of "Jipotou" was because the noodle sheets resembled a woman's headscarf, and in ancient times, women were called "jipo." They didn't even know to use Lu You's ready-made poem, nor did they try to ride on his great fame.

Just like Lu You, Bian Guanyue's belly was also bloated by the Jipotou.

She had already eaten breakfast, but she pretended she hadn't and forced down a whole bowl.

After leaving the noodle shop, Chen Guiliang carried the cat carrier and litter, walking with Bian Guanyue around West Lake to digest their food.

After strolling for over half an hour, Bian Guanyue finally said, "I'll take the cat back first. See you next semester."

"Alright, I'll walk you home," Chen Guiliang said.

The two walked side by side, soon arriving at a narrow alley. The bluestone path was worn and uneven, looking quaint and pleasant yet impoverished.

Further ahead was a construction site.

Bian Guanyue said, "The back street is being renovated into a tourist spot."

"It must be noisy on weekends then," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue said, "It's alright, it's two alleys away."

The two alleys were quickly passed.

"See you next semester!" Bian Guanyue said, a bit reluctant to part.

"See you."

Chen Guiliang took his own cat out of the carrier and put it into the shopping bag.

He hadn't bought a carrier, litter, or food for it; farm cats didn't need such things.

"Meow meow~~~"

Separated, the two kitten siblings immediately started crying out even louder.

Bian Guanyue carried her various things upstairs, pausing at the third-floor landing. Through the hollow brickwork in the wall, she watched Chen Guiliang walk further and further away.

She stood there for a long time before continuing up the stairs. The moment she got home, she called out, "Grandpa, Grandma, look what I bought?"

There was no need to look. The kitten, frightened, had been meowing non-stop.

Her grandmother laughed, "Oh my, where did this little kitten come from? It's so pretty and well-behaved."

Bian Guanyue said proudly, "You like it? I picked it out myself."

Her grandfather came over to help too. The three of them, grandparent and grandchild, busied themselves setting up a home for the kitten, pouring the litter into the box, and temporarily placing it in a corner so as not to disturb it.

The pet shop owner had said that newly bought kittens are timid.

Bian Guanyue washed her hands twice, not daring to get too close, and stood several meters away, just watching. The kitten was meowing fiercely, it must be terrified. Bian Guanyue's heart broke.

She curled up on the sofa, fiddling with the keychain she had won by West Lake, occasionally turning her head to look at the still-meowing kitten.

She couldn't hold back the smile that wanted to break out on her face.

I couldn't hold it in when I caught Old Wang either, I was grinning from ear to ear.
